message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 170, "amount_cents": 17127}, {"order_id": 175, "amount_cents": 2957}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, since the handoff is only a claim. I'll start by listing the refunds.

The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly: order 170 for 17127 and order 175 for 2957. Next I'll check the orders to confirm those refunds line up with real order amounts before computing payouts.

The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and both refunds are smaller than their order amounts (170: 17127 of 23222; 175: 2957 of 37119), so nothing looks wrong. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 11259 matches my own check (orders 28386 minus refund 17127), so the refund ledger looks consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme (11259) and birch (18633) both match my own calculations from the orders and refunds ledgers. Cobalt is the last customer with orders, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 62037 matches my check (orders 27875 + 37119 = 64994, minus refund 2957). Acme, birch, and cobalt all agree with the orders and refunds ledgers, so Alpha's refund work looks correct and I can pay. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 11259 was recorded. Birch's net of 18633 matches my check (11886 + 6747, no refunds). I'll record birch's payout next, then cobalt's.
Cobalt's payout of 62037 is the last one left. It matches my check (27875 + 37119 - 2957 = 62037), and the earlier acme and birch payouts both recorded ok, so I'll record it now.
All three customers have been paid. Acme, birch, and cobalt each matched my own check against the orders and refunds ledgers, and each record_payout returned ok.
